title: Add traffic-pattern-aware failover sentinel and regression isolator
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: existing canary detectors are sensitive to short traffic bursts and correlated infra noise which leads to noisy rollbacks during expected traffic-shape changes (jobs, migration windows, marketing spikes). This PR introduces a traffic-pattern-aware "failover sentinel" and a lightweight "regression isolator" that fuse traffic-shape signals with performance metrics to reduce false-positive rollbacks while preserving rapid recovery for real regressions.

What this PR adds: 1) Traffic-shape ingestion: a new input pipeline that classifies incoming traffic into shapes (steady, spike, ramp, batch) using a configurable window and simple clustering heuristics. 2) Multi-signal fusion: a scorer that combines latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), tail latency slope, throughput saturation, error-rate delta, and infra saturation (CPU/GPU util) into a single anomaly likelihood score. 3) Context-aware thresholds: the anomaly thresholds are adjusted by observed traffic shape and recent baseline variance; spikes reduce sensitivity to p50 swings while emphasizing p99 and error-rate. 4) Regression isolator: when a signal crosses threshold, the isolator runs a short adaptive probe (synthetic vs production-sampled traffic) to determine if degradation is systemic or limited to a traffic slice. 5) Failover policies: new rollout guard policies that recommend automated partial failovers (region/model-variant-level) with an explicit rollback window and manual-approve fallback. 6) Observability: dashboards, per-canary timeline traces, and a compact alert format for automated incident responders. 7) Tests and pipeline integration: unit tests for scorer and classifier, e2e smoke harness against the perf-sim runner, and GitHub Actions CI changes to run the canary smoke suite.

Compatibility and opt-in: the sentinel is disabled by default; teams can opt-in via canary profile YAML (examples included). Default heuristics are conservative to avoid impacting existing rollouts. Migration docs and config examples are included.

Risks and mitigations: classifier mislabeling could reduce sensitivity; mitigated by fallback to legacy detector after 10 minutes of ambiguous labels. The isolator issues synthetic probes with throttled rate to avoid user impact.

Summary: improves reliability of automated rollouts in variable-traffic environments while adding guarded automation for fast failure containment.

review_conversation: Luca: This looks promising. A couple of questions: how do you prevent probe amplification when many canaries detect anomalies simultaneously? Maya: probes are rate-limited at the tenant and global level; isolator will jitter and back off if global probe budget is near exhausted. Priya: can we get a brief on the classifier false positive rate? Maya: added unit tests and an offline evaluation (results in docs) showing <2% FPR on historical traces after conservative tuning. Owen: please add a canary profile example for high-burst latency workloads. Maya: added examples and a migration note. Luca: LGTM after addressing the probe budgeting comment. Priya: approving after docs update. CI passed on final run and I verified dashboard panels.
release_notes:
- Add traffic-pattern-aware failover sentinel: reduces false-positive rollbacks during traffic spikes.
- Introduce regression isolator with adaptive probes for deterministic rollback decisions.
- Opt-in canary profile and example configs.
- New observability dashboards and alert templates.
notes: Feature gated behind canary profile opt-in. Rollout recommended to a subset of non-critical services for 2 weeks before full adoption.
qa_steps: Enable sentinel on a test canary via config YAML
Run perf-sim smoke harness and verify no spurious rollbacks under synthetic spike traffic
Trigger an intentional p99 regression and confirm isolator recommends partial failover
